title: DNS picks the region and the balancer picks the VM
summary: A store sells to Mexico and Spain under a single domain, tienda.mx, from mx-central-1 and eu-south-2. If a region fails, shoppers must reach the other one within minutes.

requirements.1: {{s1}} publishes a single name, tienda.mx, and answers with the address of the healthy region closest to the shopper, with a 60 s TTL.
requirements.2: {{s2}} probes from several points on the internet, at a set interval, that each region's balancer answers; if one fails, slot 1 stops announcing it.
requirements.3: {{s3}} receives HTTPS in region A, terminates TLS and spreads requests only across the web VMs that pass their health check.
requirements.4: {{s4}} keeps at least 2 web VMs in region A in different zones, replaces the one that fails and adds more when the load goes up.
requirements.5: {{s5}} delivers the alarm's alert to the on-call team when slot 2 marks a region as down; the repair clock starts with that alert.
requirements.6: {{s6}} does in region B what slot 3 does in A: terminates TLS and spreads requests only across the healthy web VMs.
requirements.7: {{s7}} does what slot 4 does, for the web VMs in region B: at least 2 in different zones, replaces the one that fails and adds more with the load.

s1.explanation: With records that share a name and a latency policy, Route 53 answers with any healthy record and stops including the one it considers unhealthy (active-active failover). VPC Resolver resolves queries for VPCs; it does not publish the store.
s1.hint_cue: answers with the address of the healthy region closest

s2.explanation: Several Route 53 health checkers watch each region's endpoint; if they mark it unhealthy, Route 53 stops answering with that record. The target group health check only checks the balancer's targets.
s2.hint_cue: probes from several points on the internet

s3.explanation: The Application Load Balancer terminates HTTPS with its certificate, spreads traffic across EC2 instances in several zones and, with its target group health checks, only sends traffic to healthy targets.

s4.explanation: The EC2 Auto Scaling group watches the health of its instances and replaces the one that fails to keep the desired capacity; it also raises or lowers the number of instances with demand.
s4.hint_cue: replaces the one that fails and adds more

s5.explanation: A CloudWatch alarm on the health check publishes to an SNS topic, and SNS sends the email to the on-call team. The guide warns that several minutes can pass between the failure and the alert.
s5.hint_cue: delivers the alarm's alert to the on-call team

s6.explanation: In region B the Application Load Balancer also terminates HTTPS, spreads traffic across the EC2 instances in its zones and, with its target group health checks, only sends traffic to healthy targets.
s6.hint_cue: terminates TLS and spreads requests only across the healthy web VMs

s7.explanation: Region B has its own EC2 Auto Scaling group: it replaces the instance that fails its health check and raises or lowers the number of instances with demand.
s7.hint_cue: replaces the one that fails and adds more with the load

aws-route53-resolver.s1: VPC Resolver resolves DNS queries for VPCs and hybrid networks and forwards them to on-premises servers; it does not publish tienda.mx or stop announcing the region that fails.

aws-target-group-health-check.s2: The target group health check is run by the balancer on its registered targets, so it only sends traffic to the healthy ones; the slot asks for the Route 53 health checkers, which watch each region's endpoint so Route 53 stops answering with the unhealthy record.

aws-api-gateway.s3: API Gateway is for creating, publishing and securing REST, HTTP and WebSocket APIs; this slot must spread traffic across the region's registered instances and leave out those that fail their health check.
aws-api-gateway.s6: API Gateway is for creating, publishing and securing REST, HTTP and WebSocket APIs; this slot must spread traffic across the region's registered instances and leave out those that fail their health check.

aws-launch-template.s4: The launch template specifies the settings used to launch EC2 instances, such as the AMI, the instance type and the security groups; the slot asks for what watches their health and uses those settings to launch a replacement for the one that fails.
aws-launch-template.s7: The launch template specifies the settings used to launch EC2 instances, such as the AMI, the instance type and the security groups; the slot asks for what watches their health and uses those settings to launch a replacement for the one that fails.

aws-ec2.s4: Each web VM in the diagram is already an EC2 instance; the slot asks for what keeps the number of instances and launches a replacement when one fails or terminates.
aws-ec2.s7: Each web VM in the diagram is already an EC2 instance; the slot asks for what keeps the number of instances and launches a replacement when one fails or terminates.

aws-cloudwatch-logs.s5: CloudWatch Logs is for monitoring, storing and accessing log files; the slot asks for the topic the CloudWatch alarm sends its notification to, so the email reaches the on-call team.
